notes: Ghidra extension configures banked memory maps, ROMs, hardware registers and symbols for C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, and bundles explicit SPC700 and 65C816 language variants for SNES code. The SPC700 language is decode-capable with p-code still under rewrite; the 65C816 language is disassembly-oriented while its p-code is verified against exhaustive vectors. Current NES work resolves proven constant-pointer indirect jumps and bounds table-after-code jump tables by their switch window; Mega Man and Life Force rows were re-blessed, while Contra, Final Fantasy and TMNT changes remain held for owner review. Its exhaustive 65C816 vector baseline now reports 500 PASS, 8 N/A and 4 FAIL rows after isolating one named SBC (dp,X) test-vector oracle defect. The exception is guarded by tripwires that fail if the case starts passing or disappears, so it cannot mask wider regressions. Build and real-ROM gates therefore demonstrate bounded progress rather than universal correctness claims.

title: YoshiNESRecomp

title: z80-smart-disassembler
display_title: Z80 Smart Disassembler — CPC ROM analysis and assembler output
notes: Python Z80 disassembler developed to analyse Amstrad CPC ROMs; heuristically identifies strings/data and supports template and label files, cross references, and assembly output for several assemblers. The README documents a usable command-line interface, not a verified byte-exact source reconstruction.

title: z88dk — Z80 development kit
notes: Long-running C/assembly compiler, assembler, linker and machine libraries targeting over a hundred Z80-family machines, including CPC; one coherent toolkit at repository root.

title: Zany Kong BBC disassembly
notes: BBC Micro Zany Kong assembly listing plus original disk material and imagery, credited to Christopher Hyde and Solar Soft; source completeness and byte matching untested.

title: Zaxxon
notes: Uncommented KickAssembler source splits banked C64 Zaxxon cartridge into four CHIP sections; build scripts reassemble a 20 KB CRT while accommodating a mirrored $9000 debug bank. Documentation describes a launchable result but exact matching was not verified.

title: Zeliard
display_title: Zeliard — bit-perfect MASM reconstruction and web port
notes: Author reports release builds reproduce original DOS binaries and all three SAR archives bit for bit via build_masm.py --verify; the C/WebAssembly port is playable to the ending. Separate from awkto's independent Zeliard study and SDL port.

title: zerotape
source_language: The Great Escape C model state
notes: Structured-text C serializer built for saving and loading state in the tracked The Great Escape in C reconstruction. Uses ZT field macros and a Lemon-generated grammar; README documents integer-focused syntax and limitations. General-purpose library serving that project, not an original Spectrum tape format parser or binary-derived reconstruction.

title: ZippyRace-OCS
display_title: Zippy Race — OCS Amiga fan conversion
notes: Hand-written fan conversion of Irem's 1983 arcade Zippy Race for OCS Amiga. The README explicitly states that no reverse engineering or transcoding was performed; the game was recreated by hand in C with some assembly to match the arcade original as closely as possible. It is tracked under the broader retro-development/homebrew scope rather than as an RE-derived port.

runtime_profiles.name: OCS Amiga
runtime_profiles.notes: README states 50/60 fps on any Amiga with 1 Meg; the Makefile explicitly compiles and assembles for 68000.

evidence.excerpt: runs at 50/60fps on any Amiga with 1Meg

title: Zool 2 AGA — Amiga disassembly
notes: Complete Zool 2 AGA disassembly, described as clean enough to assemble and alter. Its workflow extracts the original disks, combines parallel IRA/disassembly strategies, rebuilds sections with vasm and tests the result with the original floppy data.

title: Zub
notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Zub directory contains an approximately 1305 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus project configuration. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

notes: Independent reproducible disassemblies of nine ZX Spectrum games. Seven are documented as 100% covered and byte-exactly reassembled: Atic Atac, Knight Lore, Pentagram, Alien 8, Nightshade, The Hobbit and Ant Attack. Builds require owner-supplied media; the original-table room editor now covers Knight Lore, Pentagram and Alien 8, while generated pages/media run the games' own routines.

title: ZX84

evidence: Recent commits contain explicit Claude Opus 5 co-author trailers.
